key_insight: Across perovskites, polar off-centering enhances low-frequency infrared and dielectric responses, while nonpolar octahedral tilting is associated with Raman central peaks.
engineering_relevance: Linking spectral signatures to lattice instabilities can help interpret structural dynamics in halide-perovskite solar-cell materials.
method: Use machine-learning-based molecular dynamics to simulate infrared and Raman spectra.
Compare seven oxide, halide and double-halide perovskites with polar, tilt-driven and mixed instabilities.
Relate low-frequency features to mode symmetry, coupling strength and dynamics.
evidence_signal: Simulations across seven compositions indicate that slow polar reorientations shift dielectric responses to very low frequencies, while overdamped tilting produces persistent Raman central peaks.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulated spectroscopy, not solar-cell performance gains or quantitative experimental validation.
paper_title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
